South East Inner City (Temple Bar, Grafton Street, Trinity College, St Stephen's Green) — Dublin, Ireland

🟡 Local press research

Average day Higher caution advised night

In detail

This LEA covers Dublin's densest tourist core — Temple Bar, Grafton Street, Trinity College and St Stephen's Green — and press coverage from 2024-2026 shows a marked gap between daytime and nighttime risk. By day, the main documented issue is petty and organised theft: Newstalk and Garda press material describe pickpocket gangs (including an 'Oliver Twist'-style operation that led to roughly 40 arrests in an undercover crackdown) specifically working Dublin city-centre tourist hotspots such as Grafton Street and Temple Bar, a long-running pattern rather than a single incident. There have also been isolated daytime/evening assaults reported near St Stephen's Green, including a Garda witness appeal after a man in his 30s was hospitalised following an assault at St Stephen's Green West on the August bank holiday Monday in 2024 (TheJournal.ie, Garda.ie). At night, however, the picture is significantly more serious. In February 2026, a man was critically injured in a violent assault in Temple Bar; two men were arrested and later charged with a 'vicious' attack, and after the victim — identified as an English tourist — died of his injuries, one of the accused was charged with murder (RTÉ, Irish Times, BreakingNews.ie, 19-27 Feb 2026). Separately, in June 2026, 21-year-old Qayyum Balogun was fatally stabbed just off Grafton Street near Clarendon Street after being chased by a large group following a row near a venue hosting a concert at Bewley's; a bystander was also stabbed in the same incident, and multiple arrests and charges followed, including of a man accused of leading a '14-man pack' that chased the victim (TheJournal.ie, RTÉ, Irish Times, June 2026). These two fatal or near-fatal nighttime attacks within months of each other, both tied to late-night/nightlife circumstances in the heart of the tourist district, represent a well-documented and serious pattern rather than an isolated event, distinct from the area's long-standing but comparatively minor daytime pickpocketing problem. No pattern of daytime muggings or serious daytime violence specifically was found beyond the theft and the isolated Stephen's Green assault, so daytime risk is rated as limited/localized (yellow) while nighttime risk, given the two 2026 homicide-related cases centred on Temple Bar and Grafton Street, is rated red. Sources checked: RTÉ (rte.ie); The Irish Times (irishtimes.com); TheJournal.ie (thejournal.ie); BreakingNews.ie (breakingnews.ie); Irish Examiner (irishexaminer.com); Newstalk (newstalk.com); An Garda Síochána (garda.ie).
